spec.description: The earthquakes under the northern Andes since 1904, from the USGS catalog, each at its depth on a 3D map seen through the ground: the Nazca plate sinking under Ecuador, Colombia and Peru, drawn by the quakes inside it. A profile of depth by longitude, a timeline that grows the catalog year by year, and the map turned inside out at a click.

options.content:
| | |
|---|---|
| Earthquakes | The USGS's [ANSS Comprehensive Catalog](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/data/comcat/) (ComCat, public domain): every earthquake between 12° S and 8° N, 84° W and 66° W with a depth and a magnitude, 12,053 from 1904 to 13 November 2026 |
| How complete | Outside the United States ComCat lists what the world's networks report: about complete from M4.5 since the 1970s, sparser and coarser before (96% of the rows are from 1973 on). A depth of exactly 10 or 33 km is often one a network fixed, not one it measured |
| Heights | Turned inside out, an earthquake stands as high as it is deep, at true scale; under the ground, it sits at its depth below a see-through ground. The stems join each earthquake deeper than 70 km of M4.5 or more to the surface above it |
| Colours | Depth: less than 35 km (the crust), 35 to 70, 70 to 150, 150 to 300, 300 km or more. Size: magnitude |
| Ground | [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/)'s 1:50m countries (public domain); base map © OpenStreetMap contributors © CARTO |
| Built by | `datasets/andes-quakes/build.sh` in [pacha-dashboards](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/pacha-dashboards) |

spec.rawSql:
-- Every earthquake at its depth: kepler lifts a point by its altitude in metres, so a depth goes down
-- (or up, turned inside out). Each row also carries its stem, from the surface to the earthquake when it
-- is deeper than 70 km and of magnitude 4.5 or more, of no length otherwise: one dataset, so the filters
-- of the shared selection reach the stems too. The profile's box (longitude by depth) is one clause over two
-- columns, which the map's link to the selection leaves out: it comes in here, from the variables it writes.
SELECT id, time, place, latitude, longitude, depth_km, mag, depth_km * 1000 * $side::DOUBLE AS altitude,
  latitude AS lat0, longitude AS lng0, latitude AS lat1, longitude AS lng1,
  CASE WHEN depth_km > 70 AND mag >= 4.5 THEN 0 ELSE depth_km * 1000 * $side::DOUBLE END AS alt0,
  depth_km * 1000 * $side::DOUBLE AS alt1
FROM $quakes
WHERE $__crossfilter($quakeFilters, -time, -area)

-- Cities on the ground, to know where you are.
SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Quito', -0.2201, -78.5123), ('Guayaquil', -2.1962, -79.8862), ('Cuenca', -2.9006, -79.0045), ('Bogotá', 4.711, -74.0721), ('Medellín', 6.2442, -75.5812), ('Cali', 3.4516, -76.532), ('Iquitos', -3.7437, -73.2516), ('Trujillo', -8.1116, -79.0288)) AS c(label, latitude, longitude)

-- The ground: the countries' land, drawn see-through over what lies under it.
SELECT country, geometry FROM $land

options.content:
## Ecuador from the inside

Something on this map is not quite right: it is **turned inside out**. Each dot is an earthquake under the northern Andes since 1904, and its height is how deep it broke. What stands in the sky is the inside of the Earth: the Nazca plate, sinking under South America, drawn by the earthquakes inside it.

Under the coast of Ecuador they break about 40 km down, under the Andes 110, under the Amazon near Palora and Macas 170, where the strongest of them struck: M7.5 in 2019. Under the border of Colombia and Peru, one broke 645 km down: M8.0 in 1970.

Switch **Seen** to *Under the ground* to put them back. Press play on the timeline; drag a box on the profile.
